title: graphify's recorded installer resolves by version and never checks the pinned wheel sha256
description: Run-4 (U150 head a2b96f8b) raised this lead: the graphify asset recorded verify: sha256 and the reviewed wheel digest, but its installer was `uv tool install graphifyy==0.9.99`, a by-version index resolve that passed no digest. Run-5 (round 3) rejected it: the installer downloads the one reviewed wheel, compares its sha256 with the pin and installs the local file. At 2329bd97 (round 4) the rejection holds and is stronger: the digest read checks shasum's status, and the asset, now keyed graphifyy with its wheel files entry, is skipped by make update's uv tool upgrade loop, so no later step replaces the verified install. At 8e3258bc (round 5) the installer is unchanged and a failure-injection test now runs it against stubs, so the rejection rests on an executed check in CI as well as on the source. At 6d2feb0e (round 6) the installer and its tests are unchanged apart from module-level agent-home isolation in the test file.
claimed_root_cause: The graphify asset's installer was a by-version index resolve with no hash input, so the entry's verify: sha256 and recorded digest bound nothing at install time.

trace.description: The operator step: mktemp, curl of the one wheel URL, sha256 read and comparison, local-file install.
h=$(shasum -a 256 <wheel>) with its status checked (|| exit 1), then [ "${h%% *}" = <pinned digest> ] at line 1347, chained by && before the install.
uv tool install --force of the verified local wheel file, reached only when the digest matched.

evidence.description: verify: sha256, with the digest at line 1320, applied by the installer.
files.any names the one wheel URL (line 1322), the .whl entry manifest_wheel_pin looks for.
The test refuses a by-version install (no graphifyy==) and requires the wheel name and shasum -a 256 (lines 179-181), download before verify before install (lines 182-187).
The test requires the status-checked digest read and no other pipe in the command (lines 198-200).
test_make_update_skips_the_pinned_tool runs upgrade-tools.sh's manifest_wheel_pin over the manifest: 0.9.99 for graphifyy, nothing for graphify (lines 202-205).
upgrade_uv_tools asks manifest_wheel_pin before `uv tool upgrade` and skips a pinned wheel tool (lines 553-557).
The same download, compare, install-the-file form as update_hcom (install at line 1699).

Round 5's failure-injection test runs the installer line against stub curl, uv and mktemp in a scratch directory: uv is reached once when the digest matches and never for mismatched bytes, a shasum that prints the pin and exits 1, or a failed curl (lines 207-229).

reason: Refuted by the current source: the recorded installer (agent-config.yaml:1385-1392) binds the reviewed digest at install time (download, status-checked shasum -a 256 compared with the pin, && before the local-file install), test_graphify_asset.py:175-205 holds that form and the make-update skip, and test_graphify_asset.py:207-229 runs the gate against stubs, and upgrade-tools.sh:552-557 never upgrades the tool afterwards. The unhashed dependency closure of the one trial `uv tool install <wheel>` is a separate, smaller residual shared with the hcom install and is recorded as hardening, not as this claim.

title: The carry digest drops every hunk position, so a head that moves an audited line elsewhere in the same file inherits the earlier head's audit verdict
description: Run-25's lead at f3a20724: the carry digest hashed zero-context hunks with their `@@` positions dropped, so a head that added or deleted the same lines at another place of a file carried the earlier head's verdict. Round 2 binds each hunk to its place; the claim fails here (see reason).
claimed_root_cause: The carry digest hashes zero-context hunks without their positions, so it equates changes that place the same lines at different places in a file, and both the carry and the fixed-under-carry rule treat digest equality as change equality.

trace.description: The carry run hashes the new head's change against its merge base.
Each path's patch is read with three lines of context.
Each hunk carries its occurrence index among the merge-base blob's equal windows.
Digest equality decides the carry.

evidence.description: occurrence_index counts the window's earlier occurrences, overlaps included.
The hunk header is kept with its numbers blanked.
The identical edit moved to a second function is not carried.
The edit at the third of three identical windows is another digest.

reason: Refuted at 23d9d28b (U180 round 2). The digest no longer drops hunk positions without a replacement: each hunk keeps three lines of context (scripts/orchestrator/audit-carry.py:702) and an `@@occurrence <n>` line, the count of earlier occurrences of its old-side window in the merge-base blob (:667-676, :759-760), so two places of one file never hash alike, while a merge of main that moves the hunk without touching its window still carries. A parent-side re-implementation over dummy repositories (run-26 agents/v26-d1/scratch/collide.txt; the lever not run) gives different digests for run-25's two pairs and for one edit in either of two identical blocks; the tests pin a moved edit and the third of three identical windows as not carried (tests/unit/test_audit_carry.py:447, :521). The claim stays suppressed only while this source is unchanged.

title: Claude Code sandbox write roots expose hcom launch inputs and seat sandbox files that later run unsandboxed
description: The managed user-level Claude Code settings grant every Claude Code session on the host sandboxed write access to ~/.local/state/hcom, ~/.local/state/hcom-regime and ~/.local/state/omp-seats, with autoAllowBashIfSandboxed true and no denyWrite. The orchestrator README records that an hcom store holds executable launch inputs (config.toml, env, config.env, scripts, integrations, .tmp/launch, shell_env.json) that the next seat launch runs outside any sandbox, and <seats-root>/.sandbox/<name>/ holds each seat's srt settings and omp shim. A Bash command auto-approved inside the sandbox of any session, including one steered by untrusted repository content, can therefore plant input that a later unsandboxed process executes. The seat sandbox denies writes to exactly these files (hcom-seat:1703-1705 and :1681); the Claude Code sandbox has no equivalent, and the manifest's own invariant says these roots hold nothing a later unsandboxed run trusts as configuration. The repository lists this as a residual (README:259). Fix if validated: add sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite entries for <store>/{config.toml,env,config.env,scripts,integrations,.tmp/launch,shell_env.json} under both hcom roots and for ~/.local/state/omp-seats/*/.sandbox (generated from the same list hcom-seat uses), with a validate-agent-assets.py invariant that every extra_allow_write root carries them.
claimed_root_cause: claude.sandbox.filesystem.extra_allow_write in home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml, rendered by scripts/generate-agent-configs.py into the user-level Claude Code settings, grants whole-directory write to the hcom store parent and the seats root without denyWrite entries for the files in them that unsandboxed processes execute or trust as configuration.

trace.description: autoAllowBashIfSandboxed true: a Bash command that runs inside the sandbox is approved without a prompt.
allowWrite lists ~/.local/state/hcom-regime, ~/.local/state/hcom and ~/.local/state/omp-seats (lines 577-579; Linux branch lines 662-664) and no denyWrite follows.
The managed template is merged into the user-level ~/.claude/settings.json, so the roots apply to every project's sessions.
Any sandboxed command can write the store's executable inputs, which the next seat launch runs outside the sandbox.

evidence.description: Manifest invariant: the extra write roots hold nothing on PATH and nothing a later unsandboxed run trusts as configuration.
extra_allow_write lists ~/.cache/uv, ~/.local/state/hcom-regime, ~/.local/state/hcom, ~/.local/state/omp-seats.
The generator renders extra_allow_write into sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite.
Seats deny writes to config.toml, env, config.env, .tmp/launch, scripts, integrations and shell_env.json in the store: the sibling control the Claude Code sandbox lacks.
Seats deny writes to <seats-root>/.sandbox, which the Claude Code sandbox can write.
Linux branch allowWrite repeats the same three roots.

blockers: hcom's consumption of config.toml, env, config.env, scripts, integrations, .tmp/launch and shell_env.json at seat launch happens in the external hcom binary; the repository only asserts it (README:259).

Whether Claude Code's sandbox (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux) grants writes to every file below an allowWrite directory when no denyWrite is set is product behavior, and this run may not execute target or agent code.

validation_plan.local: Under a scratch HOME with a dummy hcom store and the rendered settings, run one sandboxed Claude Code Bash command that appends a benign marker assignment (MARKER=1) to <scratch>/.local/state/hcom/<slug>/env; then launch a dummy seat against a fake omp that prints its environment and check whether MARKER=1 reaches the unsandboxed launch. Stop at the marker.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms from the installed hcom version which store files `hcom omp` reads or executes at launch, and checks that ~/.claude/settings.json sandbox.filesystem carries no denyWrite for them.

title: disk-gc splits worktree paths on whitespace and can rm -rf a different directory
description: The daily `disk-gc --apply` systemd user timer (Ubuntu) parses `git worktree list --porcelain` with awk `print $2`, so a worktree path containing a space is cut at the first space. When the cut prefix names an existing directory inside a checkout whose HEAD is merged and whose tree is clean (rev-parse and status then answer for the enclosing repository), or an idle clone sharing history, it passes the per-worktree checks; `git worktree remove` fails on it and the script then runs `rm -rf` on the cut path. A worktree entry needs only a .git/worktrees/<id>/gitdir file, which a sandboxed Claude Code session can create in its working repository and a Linux omp seat can create in the shared git common directory (Linux srt denies only literal existing paths, hcom-seat:1692-1693), so a contained agent could make an unsandboxed daily job delete a directory it cannot write. Only untracked files and ignored files under 1 MiB are archived first; larger ignored files and unpushed work in a deleted clone are lost. The sibling lever worktree-gc.sh already uses --porcelain -z. Fix if validated: read `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, split on NUL, require each candidate's `git -C <path> rev-parse --show-toplevel` to equal the listed path, and never rm -rf a path git did not just remove as a worktree.
claimed_root_cause: worktree_gc derives worktree paths with awk whitespace field splitting instead of NUL-delimited porcelain, and falls back to rm -rf on a path git refused to remove as a worktree.

trace.description: Runs disk-gc --apply unsandboxed as the user; the timer fires daily (disk-gc.timer.tmpl:5).
worktrees=$(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree / { print $2 }') keeps only the text before the first space of each path.
The cut path passes [ -d ] when that prefix directory exists.
git -C <cut path> rev-parse HEAD answers for the enclosing repository, and the merge, status, recency and lock checks follow on that basis (lines 189-210).
git worktree remove --force --force fails for a path that is not a worktree; the failure is only logged.
rm -rf on the cut path because the directory still exists.

evidence.description: OnCalendar daily at 04:00.
chezmoi apply enables the timer with systemctl --user enable --now.
main_wt is derived with the same awk $2 split.
The lock check uses the basename of the cut path, which normally has no lock file.
The sibling lever reads git worktree list --porcelain -z.
On Linux, srt write denies are literal existing paths only, so a worktree admin entry created after launch is not denied.

blockers: Proof needs git and disk-gc to run against a fixture repository; this run may not execute target code and used no OS sandbox.
Whether the installed git prints a worktree path containing a space unquoted in --porcelain output (without -z) needs that run.

validation_plan.local: In a scratch HOME on Linux with DISK_GC_WORKSPACE set to a scratch directory: create repository A with an origin/main, a tracked directory keep/ whose files are older than four days, and a worktree admin entry whose gitdir names <A>/keep x/.git; run disk-gc without --apply and confirm it logs `remove keep`, then run with --apply inside the sandbox and confirm keep/ is removed. Stop there.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner runs disk-gc in report mode (no --apply) on the Ubuntu host and checks for any remove line naming a path that `git worktree list --porcelain -z` does not list.

title: The DeepSeek harness installer resolves the thak profile's plugins from the npm registry with no lockfile, outside the reviewed digest
description: update_deepseek_harness verifies GitHub's tag archive of the harness against a reviewed sha256 and builds it from its own lockfile, but then runs `mise exec -- pnpm install` in the deployed thak profile directory (scripts/update-agent-assets.sh:2009) with no lockfile and no --frozen-lockfile. The profile's only dependency, @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code at 0.2.1-rc.5 (home/dot_dsh/profiles/thak/package.json:14), therefore comes from the npm registry, not from the verified archive, and its own dependencies resolve to whatever versions their ranges admit at install time; the kit renders no lockfile for the profile (scripts/generate-agent-configs.py:2595-2596). That code is loaded into the harness and runs as the operator whenever dsh starts (and at install if pnpm runs its dependencies' lifecycle scripts). The repository's npm cooldown, min-release-age=3 (home/dot_npmrc:1), is npm's key; pnpm 12.8.1 from mise performs this install. A malicious or hijacked release of any package in that closure, inside its range and younger than any cooldown pnpm applies, would run on every opted-in host at its next harness install. Fix if validated: commit a generated pnpm-lock.yaml for the profile (or install the hooks plugin from the verified archive's own workspace) and run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` there, and set pnpm's own minimum-release-age for the profile install.
claimed_root_cause: The profile's plugin install resolves its dependency closure fresh at install time, outside the archive digest and the archive's lockfile that bind the harness itself.

trace.description: make update runs update_deepseek_harness on every host; it proceeds only where DSH_HOME is exported and names ~/.dsh.
The reviewed sha256 binds the downloaded harness archive only.
The harness builds from its digest-bound lockfile with --frozen-lockfile.
The profile's plugins install with `mise exec -- pnpm install`, no lockfile and no --frozen-lockfile.

evidence.description: The one dependency, the Claude hooks plugin, an exact prerelease version from the npm registry.
The rendered profile scope names package.json and cordis.patch.yml only; no lockfile is rendered.
The lockfile pnpm writes in the deployed profile is an unmanaged byproduct the doctor is told to ignore.
The repository's npm cooldown is npm's own key, min-release-age.
pnpm comes from mise as npm:pnpm 12.8.1.
The Understand-Anything build in the same file tries pnpm install --frozen-lockfile first.

blockers: Whether pnpm 12.8.1 applies ~/.npmrc's min-release-age (npm's key) or only its own minimum-release-age setting is pnpm behaviour, not visible in this repository.

The dependency ranges of @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code@0.2.1-rc.5, whether pnpm runs their lifecycle scripts, and whether the harness loads the plugin from the profile's node_modules or from its own verified workspace are facts of the registry and the upstream harness.

validation_plan.local: In a scratch HOME with an empty pnpm store, copy home/dot_dsh/profiles/thak/package.json into an empty directory and run `mise exec npm:pnpm@12.8.1 -- pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts`; read the written pnpm-lock.yaml for packages resolved through ranges and for versions published less than three days before, and `pnpm config get minimum-release-age`. Stop at the lockfile; build and run nothing.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner reads the published manifest of @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code@0.2.1-rc.5 and the harness's plugin resolution, and decides whether the profile gets a committed lockfile.

title: The kit's only DeepSeek harness profile turns the harness's command sandbox off, and nothing makes a dsh run happen inside an srt seat
description: The rendered thak profile disables the harness's own command-isolation row, bash-sandbox (home/dot_dsh/profiles/thak/cordis.patch.yml:9-10), and the asset's note gives the reason: 'the seat boundary is srt or nothing' (home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml:1351). No code of this head provides that seat: scripts/orchestrator/hcom-seat starts only omp seats (:3-11), no lever starts dsh, and the wrapper update_deepseek_harness installs at ~/.dsh/bin/dsh execs the harness directly under mise's node with no seat check (scripts/update-agent-assets.sh:2003). Every run of the installed harness is therefore 'nothing': a session driven by a cloud model over ollama.com (cordis.patch.yml:14-18), reading repository and tool content that may carry injected instructions, runs its shell tool on the operator's account with the operator's credentials and no isolation, which is the outcome the repository refuses for Claude Code (agent-config.yaml:916-921, failIfUnavailable). Whether a command runs without an approval prompt under the headless bundle decides how much of this is reachable. What the Claude hooks plugin the profile mounts over ~/.claude/settings.json (cordis.patch.yml:22-26) enforces on the shell tool, the kit's permission gate permgate among its hooks (home/.chezmoitemplates/claude-settings-managed.json:786-792), is upstream behaviour this head does not pin; U179's coverage test, which pins it as no gate at dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5, is a separate commit not in this head (run-23). Fix if validated: keep bash-sandbox enabled in the kit profile and disable it only in a seat overlay, or make ~/.dsh/bin/dsh refuse to start outside an srt seat (for example when HCOM_SEAT_SANDBOX is unset), the way hcom-seat refuses to launch without srt.
claimed_root_cause: The profile disables the harness's command sandbox on the premise of an srt seat boundary that no launch path of this head applies.

trace.description: The installed wrapper starts the harness directly under mise's node; it checks for no seat.
The profile composes the headless bundle.
The harness's own command-isolation row is disabled in every run of the profile.

evidence.description: The asset's note: its own command sandbox is off since the seat boundary is srt or nothing.
The seat launcher starts omp seats through hcom omp, nothing else.
The model behind the session is served from ollama.com.
Claude Code is configured to refuse to start rather than run commands unsandboxed.
The test asserts the sandbox row disabled by id.
The kit's permission gate is a PermissionRequest hook that runs permgate.

blockers: Whether the dsh headless bundle asks for approval before its shell tool runs a command, or runs it, is behaviour of the upstream harness at dsh-v0.2.1-rc.5.

What @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code enforces from ~/.claude/settings.json (whether the PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks, permgate among them, gate the harness's shell tool) is upstream plugin behaviour; this head holds no measurement of it.

validation_plan.local: On a scratch account with no credentials and a scratch HOME, install the pinned harness with DSH_HOME=~/.dsh and point a scratch copy of the patch's ollama-cloud baseURL at a local stub that answers one tool call running `touch "$HOME/dsh-probe"`; start ~/.dsh/bin/dsh with the thak profile and observe whether it prompts, refuses or runs the command, and whether a PreToolUse hook (matchers Bash and bash) or the PermissionRequest hook in the scratch ~/.claude/settings.json is called. Stop at the probe file.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner states whether dsh is to run only inside an srt seat; if so, the wrapper or a launcher enforces it, or the kit profile keeps bash-sandbox on outside seats.

title: Bus sender identity is caller-asserted while the seats treat a row's from as identity
description: The bus trust boundary (README:177) states that identities are hcom participant names, the from and delivered_to of a row, and that no seat writes under $HCOM_DIR except through hcom. hcom-dispatch sets from from its own argument (`--from <from>` is the external sender identity), and every seat's srt settings grant write access to the whole hcom store with only its launch inputs denied, so hcom.db is seat-writable and `hcom send --from` is reachable. A worker seat can plausibly post a row whose from names the coordinator or another seat; the omp stop gate already decides a seat's task state by from. The effect on a recipient is bounded by the rule that bus text never authorises a command, but the orchestrator seat writes the main checkout and acts on TASK and RESULT lines by sender. Fix if validated: deny seats direct write to hcom.db (only hcom, binding the sender to the launched participant, should write it) or have recipients and the stop gate verify from against hcom's process binding rather than the row value.
claimed_root_cause: The bus identity seats rely on is supplied by the sender (hcom send --from, or a direct row write to the seat-writable hcom.db) instead of being bound by hcom to the launched seat.

trace.description: HCOM_DIR, the program's store, is a write root of every seat.
Only the store's launch inputs are denied; hcom.db stays writable.
hcom send ... --from "${from}" with a caller-chosen from.
The stop gate decides a task's open or closed move by comparing the row's from with the seat name.

evidence.description: Bus trust boundary: identities are the row's from and delivered_to, and no seat writes under $HCOM_DIR except through hcom.
Documents --from <from> as the external sender identity that becomes the row's from.
The store is also in every seat's allowRead.
The orchestrator seat runs approvalMode yolo.

blockers: Whether hcom accepts --from naming another participant from inside a launched seat, and whether a row written directly into hcom.db is delivered with that from, is behavior of the external hcom binary.
How the orchestrator and worker seats weigh from when acting on a line is runtime model behavior, observable only in a seat run.

validation_plan.local: With two dummy seats on a scratch HCOM_DIR, from seat B run `hcom send @seatA --from coordinator -- PING test` and, separately inside B's srt sandbox, insert a message row with from=coordinator into the scratch hcom.db with sqlite3; check what sender seat A's delivery and bus-history.sh show. Stop at the delivered row.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner checks in the installed hcom version whether send honors --from for a launched participant and whether it binds the sender to HCOM_PROCESS_ID.

title: Orchestrator seat can rewrite the Python package that the checkout's Claude Code project hooks import
description: For the orchestrator role the seat directory is the main checkout (hcom-seat:1151), and its srt settings deny writes to .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/hooks because those run outside the seat. The checkout's tracked .claude/settings.json registers SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and other hooks as `python3 ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py`; that 13-line shim puts .claude/contextdb first on sys.path and imports contextdb.hook. .claude/contextdb/contextdb/*.py is not denied, so the orchestrator seat (approvalMode yolo, reading worker pull requests and bus text) can change the code that every Claude Code session opened in the checkout, such as the coordinator's, runs as unsandboxed hooks. Worker seats have the same gap in their own worktrees. Fix if validated: add <base>/.claude/contextdb (or the whole <base>/.claude directory) to the deny_write loop at hcom-seat:1682-1684, with a regression test asserting the rendered settings carry it.
claimed_root_cause: The deny_write loop protects the hook registration and the hooks/ shims but not the package directory those shims import from, so the protection does not cover the code the hooks execute.

trace.description: orchestrator) dir=${repo}: the main checkout is the orchestrator seat's first write root.
Per base (seat directory and checkout) only .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/hooks, .omp, .codex, .envrc and .mcp.json are denied.
Project hook runs python3 with ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/contextdb_hook.py; the same command is registered for the other hook events.
sys.path.insert(0, <repo>/.claude/contextdb) before importing contextdb.hook (line 10).
Hook entry point executed from the seat-writable package directory.

evidence.description: from contextdb.hook import main: the imported module lives under the undenied .claude/contextdb.
The function's stated intent (lines 1647-1648): deny agent configuration that runs outside the seat.
The orchestrator seat runs approvalMode yolo.
seat_write_roots starts with the seat directory itself.

blockers: Whether the operator or coordinator runs Claude Code with this project's hooks enabled in the main checkout (or in a worker worktree) is a deployment fact.
srt's effective write permission below the seat directory for paths not in denyWrite needs a sandboxed run, which this run may not perform.

Stop there.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms whether Claude Code sessions are opened in the main checkout with the project's .claude/settings.json hooks trusted, and compares .claude/contextdb in the checkout with origin/main after orchestrator seat sessions.

title: Seat srt sandbox can write the operator's Claude Code config (~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/rules) that unsandboxed Claude Code sessions load
description: hcom-seat gives every omp seat (worker and orchestrator, both approvalMode yolo) write access to the operator's ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude} and ~/.claude.json so the pi-claude-bridge's Claude Code child can write its state. Inside ~/.claude it denies settings.json, settings.local.json, hooks, plugins, commands, agents, skills and CLAUDE.md, but ~/.claude.json is a write root with no deny and ~/.claude/rules is not in the deny list. ~/.claude.json holds the operator's user-scope MCP server definitions (README:173), whose commands Claude Code starts as processes; ~/.claude/rules/*.md is the user-level rules directory this repository deploys and Claude Code loads into every session. A seat steered by repository or bus content could add an MCP server command or a standing instruction that the operator's next unsandboxed Claude Code session, such as the coordinator's, runs or follows, crossing from srt containment to the operator's account. Fix if validated: give the bridge child a per-seat CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under <seats-root>/.state/<name> and drop ~/.claude.json and the operator's config directory from seat_write_roots; at minimum add rules, output-styles and projects to the deny loop and stop granting ~/.claude.json, with a regression test on the rendered srt settings.
claimed_root_cause: seat_write_roots shares the operator's own Claude Code configuration directory and ~/.claude.json with every seat, and the deny loop enumerates only some of the files Claude Code executes or loads as instructions.

trace.description: The seat's write roots include ${claude} (the operator's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude) and ${HOME}/.claude.json (continued on line 1370).
The srt allowWrite list is exactly seat_write.
Denied under ${claude}: settings.json, settings.local.json, hooks, plugins, commands, agents, skills, CLAUDE.md; nothing for rules/ and no deny for the ~/.claude.json file root.
A Claude Code child of the bridge writes ~/.claude.json, which also lists the operator's MCP servers.

evidence.description: claude=${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-${HOME}/.claude}: the operator's directory, inherited from the launcher, not a per-seat one.
The function's stated intent (lines 1647-1648): deny agent configuration that runs outside the seat.
Worker write table lists ~/.claude (minus the denied names) and ~/.claude.json.
The repository maps home/dot_claude/rules/*.md.tmpl to ~/.claude/rules/*.md, relying on Claude Code loading that directory.
Worker seats run approvalMode yolo; the srt sandbox is their only containment.

blockers: Whether Claude Code starts user-scope mcpServers from ~/.claude.json without a prompt and outside its Bash sandbox, and loads every ~/.claude/rules/*.md into sessions, is product behavior not visible in this repository.
Whether srt grants writes into the ~/.claude.json file root and below the allowed ~/.claude directory for names absent from denyWrite needs a sandboxed run, which this run may not perform.

validation_plan.local: In a scratch HOME, render a seat's srt settings with hcom-seat's seat_sandbox_write; inside `srt --settings <file>` add a dummy user-scope MCP server whose command writes a marker file into scratch, and drop a rules file with a harmless marker sentence into <scratch>/.claude/rules/; then start Claude Code with that HOME outside srt and check `claude mcp list`, the marker file, and whether the sentence appears in the loaded memory. Stop there.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects ~/.claude.json mcpServers and ~/.claude/rules on a seat host after seat sessions for entries no operator added, and confirms the installed Claude Code version's startup behavior for user-scope MCP servers.
